stories.title: Bakkafrost Q3 operating profit rose but missed forecasts, shares fell, and it ended outside smolt buying in Scotland.
stories.summary: Operational EBIT was DKK 128m (about €17m), up from DKK 22m a year earlier, helped by Faroese and FOF segment growth and narrower Scottish losses. Low harvest volumes and high costs in Scotland still weighed, and the result missed expectations, with shares down 5.6%. The company stopped external smolt sourcing in Scotland after biological setbacks and targets a 40% harvest rebound, while leaning further into the US market.

stories.title: Norwegian industry groups warn that tradable lice quotas and a lice tax could devastate the sector.
stories.summary: A new Menon report concludes that fees and tradable quotas could regulate lice emissions more precisely, and it proposes a five-year phase-in. Sjømat Norge says the rules could wreck the industry, Sjømatbedriftene expects more consolidation and less value creation along the coast, and smaller farmers fear being pushed out. Industry voices also demand an independent review, say the proposals rest on inadequate knowledge, and urge scrapping the biomass caps.

top.why: Bakkafrost's Q3 operational EBIT of DKK 128m missed forecasts and shares fell 5.6%, as low Scottish harvests and high costs weighed, while it targets a 40% harvest rebound.
Brazil is weighing a VAT of up to 26.5% on salmon, which hangs over a Chilean salmon trade worth about €900m.
A Menon report proposes lice fees and tradable quotas with a five-year phase-in, while Sjømat Norge warns the rules could wreck the industry and smaller farmers fear being pushed out.
Peru's cancelled anchovy season leaves a 6-month fishmeal and fish oil supply gap, lifting fishmeal prices and sending Chinese buyers looking for alternatives.
Norwegian export prices rose 2.7% as volumes recovered in late October, but the first November salmon saw a price drop.
